questions.hint: A round bracket means the endpoint is NOT included.

steps.explain: A round bracket \((\) means the endpoint is excluded (strict inequality).
\((6, infty)\) means all \(x\) greater than 6 (not including 6).

questions.hint: Square bracket at 4 means 4 is included.

steps.explain: \([4, infty)\) starts at 4 with a square bracket — 4 is included.
\(x > -4\) means \(x\) is strictly greater than \(-4\) — \(-4\) is not included.
Excluded endpoint \(-4\) → round bracket. Extending to \(+\infty\).

questions.hint: \(\ge\) means the endpoint IS included → square bracket.

steps.explain: \(x \ge -3\): \(-3\) is included (\(\ge\)) → square bracket.
\(x \ge 6\): 6 included → square bracket; extends to \(+\infty\).

questions.hint: OR combines two separate intervals with \(\cup\).
